title: Qwen4-Max: Alibaba's Flagship Arrives Pricier Than the Models It Chases
summary: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max is its most capable model yet and the first Qwen4 anyone outside the lab can use, but on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it lands mid-pack at 43 — 12 points behind a GPT-6.1 Sol that costs far less per task.
content:
On November 16, Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, the flagship of its Qwen4 line. It is the company's most capable model to date, and the first Qwen4 model anyone outside the lab can actually use. But the independent numbers tell a less flattering story than the launch framing. On the standard yardstick, Qwen4-Max lands in the middle of the pack while charging like a leader.

What shipped

Qwen4-Max accepts text, image, and video, returns text, and carries a 984k-token context window — close to a million tokens, or roughly 1,475 pages of dense input. Reasoning is on by default, with effort levels of none, low, high, and xhigh (high is the default), plus tool calling and structured outputs. On OpenRouter it lists at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, with cache hits at a 95% discount.

Two things stand out. First, it is proprietary. Alibaba built its reputation on open weights, and the open-weight Qwen4 models it has promised are not out yet; this Max tier is closed. Second, the price is ordinary for a frontier model — which would be fine if the capability were.

Where it actually lands

Artificial Analysis puts Qwen4-Max at 43 on its Intelligence Index, against a median of 41. That is above average. It is also 12 points behind GPT-6.1 Sol, which is cheaper to run per task.

Model Intelligence Index Cost per task Time per task
Qwen4-Max 43 $3.27 31.9 min
GPT-6.1 Sol (max) 55 $1.27 23.1 min
Gemini 4 Hydrogen (xhigh) 54 a fraction of that fast
Claude Fable 5.2 (max) 65 $26.54 40.8 min

Read the first two rows together and the problem is clear. GPT-6.1 Sol scores 55 and costs $1.27 per index task. Qwen4-Max scores 43 and costs $3.27 — about 2.6 times as much for 12 points less. Alibaba has improved its absolute position, but it is not competing on the axis that now decides most purchasing.

Slow and verbose

Cost per task is not just the sticker price. Qwen4-Max is notably slow and notably talkative. It takes 31.9 minutes per index task against a 13-minute median, and its time to first answer token runs near 148 seconds. It also emits 127M tokens during the evaluation, versus a 78.6M median — verbose output is expensive output, and verbosity is exactly what inflates the bill.

The reasoning dial is the obvious lever. Dropping from the default high effort to low cuts thinking and cost, but you are then paying a premium for a model you have to hold back to make affordable.

The release to actually watch

Alibaba's edge has been open weights, and that is where the more interesting number sits. An open Qwen 3.8 27B from August scores within a few points of Qwen4-Max on at least one analyst benchmark, costs less, and runs on desktop hardware. Testers have been blunt about the comparison: the small open model is the one they reach for. The promised open Qwen4 releases, when they land, are likely to matter more than this flagship.

Takeaway

For two years the question was "how smart is it?" The question now is "how much intelligence per dollar?" Qwen4-Max adds capability to Alibaba's lineup but loses on price-performance: on the same index, GPT-6.1 Sol does more for less, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen undercuts nearly everyone. Unless you specifically need a near-million-token multimodal context or Alibaba-native deployment, this flagship is hard to justify. The open 27B is the release worth waiting for.

Sources: Artificial Analysis, model pages for Qwen4 Max, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Claude Fable 5.2 (November 2026); OpenRouter, Qwen4 Max listing; Alibaba Qwen blog, "Qwen4-Max" (November 16, 2026).
